title: Grade 6 Science — Thu, May 28
description: Components of Food — Day 4 of 5: Deficiency diseases and vitamins
subject: science

questions.question: Deficiency diseases are caused by:
options: Lack of one or more essential nutrients in the diet over time
questions.explanation: Deficiency diseases result from long-term lack of a specific nutrient (like iron, vitamins, calcium) in the diet.

questions.question: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency causes scurvy — symptoms include bleeding gums, loose teeth, skin bruising, and poor wound healing.

questions.question: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency (along with calcium) causes rickets in children — bones become soft and bend, causing bow legs and stunted growth.

questions.question: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed for producing rhodopsin (visual pigment in eyes). Deficiency causes inability to see well in dim light (night blindness).

questions.question: Anaemia (low haemoglobin) is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to produce haemoglobin. Iron deficiency causes anaemia — symptoms are fatigue, pale skin, weakness, and breathlessness.

questions.question: Beriberi is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency causes beriberi — a disease affecting the nervous system and heart, common in populations eating mostly polished rice.

questions.question: Goitre (swelling of neck/thyroid gland) is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency causes the thyroid gland to enlarge (goitre). Iodised salt prevents this.

questions.question: Sailors on long voyages in the past often got scurvy because:
options: They had no fresh fruits and vegetables (Vitamin C sources) at sea for months
questions.explanation: Long sea voyages with no fresh produce meant no Vitamin C for months. British sailors were eventually given limes (hence 'limeys') to prevent scurvy.

questions.question: Which vitamin is MADE by our skin when exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Skin synthesises Vitamin D when exposed to UV rays in sunlight. This is why some call it the 'sunshine vitamin'.

questions.question: Kwashiorkor is a disease caused by:
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor occurs when a child's diet lacks protein. Symptoms include swollen belly (oedema), discoloured hair, skin rashes, and growth failure.

questions.question: Which vegetables are RICHEST in Vitamin A (beta-carotene)?
questions.explanation: Orange/yellow vegetables are rich in beta-carotene, which the body converts to Vitamin A. Carrots, pumpkin, and sweet potato are excellent sources.

questions.question: Why do we need to eat Vitamin C-containing foods DAILY (unlike Vitamin A)?
options: Vitamin C is water-soluble — not stored in the body, so must be replenished daily
Vitamin A is too dangerous to eat daily
Vitamin C is only found in rare foods
questions.explanation: Water-soluble vitamins (B and C) cannot be stored. Any excess is excreted in urine. You must eat fresh sources regularly.

questions.question: Which set of foods would BEST prevent night blindness?
options: Carrots, eggs, leafy greens (Vitamin A-rich foods)
questions.explanation: Night blindness is caused by Vitamin A deficiency. Carrots (beta-carotene), eggs, liver, and leafy greens are rich in Vitamin A.

questions.question: In India, iodised salt is used to prevent:
questions.explanation: Adding iodine to common salt (iodisation) is a public health measure to prevent iodine deficiency and goitre.

questions.question: Which is NOT a deficiency disease?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite (transmitted by mosquitoes) — it is an infectious disease, NOT a deficiency disease.
